findings.source_quote: Εἰς Ἰουδαίαν πορεύσομαι, ἵνα ἴδω εἰ ταῦθ’ οὗτος λέγων ἀληθεύει. ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ
findings.english_quote: “I will travel to Judea so that I may see whether this man is telling the truth in saying these things—namely, that the Son of God has come to Judea
findings.issue: The draft combines two unsettled decisions: it makes ὡς ὅτι an appositional “namely, that,” and it extends the imagined quotation through the section’s remaining explanation. This attributes material to the imagined speaker that may instead belong to the narrator. The supplied full stop after ἀληθεύει does not conclusively establish the quotation’s endpoint, but neither does it support merging the sentences with an explanatory dash. The uncertainty is disclosed in source_issues; that disclosure does not establish the chosen attribution.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the sentence break after ἀληθεύει. For fresh review, consider closing the imagined quotation after “whether this man is telling the truth in saying these things” and presenting the following explanation separately. Compare a reported-content interpretation of ὡς ὅτι with an explanatory or causal interpretation, retaining the alternative in a note. Any revised quotation boundary requires fresh review. This is a discourse-interpretation problem, not a demonstrated transcription defect.

findings.source_quote: ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος
findings.english_quote: the time of which I had once been robbed while being tossed about by hopes
findings.issue: “Robbed of the time” requires both a particular sense of εἰσεκλάπην and an analysis of χρόνον as a retained object of deprivation. The supplied construction does not establish those assumptions. An accusative of time with a passive sense involving being drawn in or beguiled remains a competing analysis. The existing source_issues disclosure correctly identifies an unresolved lexical and syntactic problem, but the main rendering cannot yet be certified. This is not evidence that the image-checked Greek is corrupt, and it is separate from the disclosed full stop after καὶ.
findings.suggested_revision: Obtain lexical evidence for εἰσκλέπτω and comparable passive constructions, especially their treatment of an accusative of time. Compare the present rendering with the provisional candidate “the time during which I had been drawn in, tossed about by hopes.” Establish the function of ποτε as part of that analysis. Preserve the supplied Greek without emendation; no renewed print verification is required merely because the construction is unfamiliar. Any replacement must undergo fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ παρὰ πολλῶν τῶν κἀκεῖθεν ἐληλυθότων ἠκούσαμεν
findings.english_quote: we have heard from many who had come from there too
findings.issue: The draft represents the καί contained in κἀκεῖθεν with “too,” but leaves the separate καὶ before παρὰ πολλῶν unrepresented. That additive marks testimony from numerous arrivals as additional corroboration, alongside the report already mentioned.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review, render “we have also heard from many of those who had come from there too,” or use another idiomatic formulation that preserves both additive expressions.
